worked_solution:
The extrema of the velocity $v$ occur at the critical points of $v.$  

Since $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=a(t),$ to find the times where $v$ is a maximum, we just need to solve $a(t)=0$ and test each solution using the first or second derivative test.

Solving $a(t)=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =0 \\ 10\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) & =0 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) & =0 \\ 5t & =\pi n \\ t & =\frac{\pi }{5}n,\end{aligned}
$$

where $n$ is any integer.  

Therefore, the extrema of the velocity function, for $t>0,$ are

$$
t=\frac{\pi }{5},\frac{2\pi }{5},\frac{3\pi }{5},…
$$

We now test the extrema values, starting with the least, using the second derivative test. For this, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}v}{\text{d}{t}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(10\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)) \\  & =50\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t).\end{aligned}
$$

At $t=\frac{\pi }{5},$ the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{5}) & =50\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\cdot \frac{\pi }{5}) \\  & =50\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ) \\  & =-50<0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${v}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{5})<0,$ we conclude that the velocity is maximized when $t=\frac{\pi }{5}.$ Therefore, the first time when the particle reaches its maximum velocity is $t=\frac{\pi }{5}\,\text{s}.$

Now, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int 10\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\text{d}t \\  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0)=2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)+C & =2 \\ -2+C & =2 \\ C & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is

$$
v(t)=4-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t).
$$

Finally, we calculate the maximum velocity:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{\text{max}} & =v(\frac{\pi }{5}) \\  & =4-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\cdot \frac{\pi }{5}) \\  & =4-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ) \\  & =6\,\text{m}/\text{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the maximum velocity  ${v}_{\text{max}}=6\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ is reached first time at  $t=\frac{\pi }{5}\,\text{s}.$

We now test the extrema values, starting with the least, using the second derivative test. For this, we compute

d2vdt2=ddt(10sin⁡(5t))=50cos⁡(5t).

At t=π5, the second derivative is

v″(π5)=50cos⁡(5⋅π5)=50cos⁡(π)=−50<0.

Since v″(π5)<0, we conclude that the velocity is maximized when t=π5. Therefore, the first time when the particle reaches its maximum velocity is t=π5s.

Now, we find v(t) by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫10sin⁡(5t)dt=−2cos⁡(5t)+C.

To determine C, we use the fact that v(0)=2. Substituting this into the above gives

−2cos⁡(0)+C=2−2+C=2C=4.

Therefore, the velocity v of the particle at time t is
v(t)=4−2cos⁡(5t).

Finally, we calculate the maximum velocity:

vmax=v(π5)=4−2cos⁡(5⋅π5)=4−2cos⁡(π)=6m/s.

So the maximum velocity vmax=6m/s is reached first time at t=π5s.
